qe: When the British government made its initial decision to partition Bengal public in December 1903, what structural composition was proposed for the western province?
qh: जब ब्रिटिश सरकार ने दिसंबर 1903 में बंगाल के विभाजन के अपने प्रारंभिक निर्णय को सार्वजनिक किया, तो पश्चिमी प्रांत के लिए क्या संरचनात्मक संयोजन प्रस्तावित किया गया था?
o: Western Bengal along with the provinces of Bihar and Orissa
Bengal proper combined exclusively with the Assam valley
Calcutta grouped with the eastern districts of Dacca and Chittagong
Western Bengal merged entirely into the Central Provinces layout
e: Detailed Explanation: The initial partition blueprint made public in December 1903 split the territory into two administrative setups: one was 'Bengal' comprising Western Bengal as well as the provinces of Bihar and Orissa, and the other was 'Eastern Bengal and Assam'.

qe: What was the total population parameter of undivided Bengal in 1903, which the colonial government officially cited as too vast to be administered efficiently by a single baseline framework?
qh: 1903 में अविभाजित बंगाल की कुल जनसंख्या का पैमाना क्या था, जिसे औपनिवेशिक सरकार ने आधिकारिक तौर पर एक ही प्रशासनिक ढांचे द्वारा कुशलतापूर्वक प्रबंधित करने के लिए बहुत विशाल बताया था?
o: 78 million
54 million
31 million
17 million
e: Detailed Explanation: The official justification provided by the British government for the partition plan was administrative necessity. They stated that Bengal, with a massive population of 78 million (roughly one-fourth of the entire population of British India), had become too large to be governed efficiently.

qe: The British partition plan strategically aimed to reduce native Bengalis to a minority within Bengal proper by balancing them against which linguistic majorities?
qh: ब्रिटिश विभाजन योजना का रणनीतिक उद्देश्य मूल बंगालियों को किस भाषाई बहुमत के सामने संतुलित करके खुद बंगाल के भीतर ही अल्पसंख्यक बनाना था?
o: Hindi and Oriya speakers tracking 37 million
Assamese and Santhali speakers accumulating 54 million
Urdu and Punjabi linguistic populations hitting 31 million
Telugu and Marathi speaking communities forming 17 million
e: Detailed Explanation: The real motive was to weaken Bengal, the nerve center of Indian nationalism. It sought to divide the population linguistically, reducing the Bengalis to a minority within their own province by grouping 17 million Bengali speakers with 37 million Hindi and Oriya speakers in the western half.

qe: Under the religious division metrics engineered by the partition, what was the estimated demographic layout designed for the western half of Bengal?
qh: विभाजन द्वारा तैयार किए गए धार्मिक विभाजन के मानकों के तहत, बंगाल के पश्चिमी हिस्से के लिए अनुमानित जनसांख्यिकीय संरचना क्या तय की गई थी?
o: A Hindu majority area with 42 million out of a total 54 million
A Muslim majority area containing 18 million out of 31 million
An equal baseline balance of 17 million Hindus and 17 million Muslims
A Buddhist dominated province tracking close to 78 million residents
e: Detailed Explanation: Religiously, the partition plan structured the western half as a Hindu-majority zone containing 42 million Hindus out of a total population of 54 million, while the eastern half was designed as a Muslim-majority province.

qe: According to the colonial religious demographic mapping, the newly proposed province of Eastern Bengal and Assam was structured to have what specific communal majority?
qh: औपनिवेशिक धार्मिक जनसांख्यिकीय मानचित्रण के अनुसार, पूर्वी बंगाल और असम के नए प्रस्तावित प्रांत को किस विशिष्ट सांप्रदायिक बहुमत के लिए तैयार किया गया था?
o: A Muslim majority area with 18 million out of a total of 31 million
A Hindu majority block capturing 42 million out of 54 million
An absolute animist majority tracking near 78 million individuals
A Christian dominated tribal belt managed entirely by direct jurisdiction
e: Detailed Explanation: The eastern province, designated as Eastern Bengal and Assam with Dacca as its capital, was structured to have a distinct Muslim majority consisting of 18 million Muslims out of a total population of 31 million.

qe: Which British Home Secretary to the Government of India recorded a note in 1904 stating: 'Bengal united is a power. Bengal divided will pull in several different ways... One of our main objects is to split up... opponents to our rule.'?
qh: भारत सरकार के किस ब्रिटिश गृह सचिव ने 1904 में एक नोट में लिखा था: 'संयुक्त बंगाल एक शक्ति है। विभाजित बंगाल कई अलग-अलग तरीकों से खींचेगा... हमारा मुख्य उद्देश्य हमारे शासन के विरोधियों को विभाजित करना है।'?
o: Risley
Curzon
Wellesley
Adams
e: Detailed Explanation: Herbert Hope Risley, the Home Secretary to the Government of India, candidly documented the true political motive of the partition plan in his official minutes in 1904, explicitly stating that the goal was to split up a solid body of nationalist opponents.

qe: Who among the following triplet of early nationalist leaders spearheaded the anti-partition campaign under the Moderate methodology during the initial phase between 1903 and 1905?
qh: 1903 और 1905 के बीच प्रारंभिक चरण के दौरान नरमपंथी कार्यप्रणाली के तहत विभाजन-विरोधी अभियान का नेतृत्व निम्नलिखित में से किस शुरुआती राष्ट्रवादी नेता की त्रिमूर्ति ने किया था?
o: Surendranath Banerjea, K.K. Mitra, and Prithwishchandra Ray
Bal Gangadhar Tilak, Lala Lajpat Rai, and Bipin Chandra Pal
Aurobindo Ghosh, Ajit Singh, and Syed Haider Raza
Dadabhai Naoroji, Dinshaw Wacha, and W.C. Bonnerjee
e: Detailed Explanation: During the initial phase (1903–1905), leadership was firmly held by the Moderates, specifically Surendranath Banerjea, K.K. Mitra, and Prithwishchandra Ray, who relied on constitutional agitation methods.

qe: The early anti-partition agitation launched by the Moderate leadership between 1903 and 1905 relied heavily on which communicative tool to generate public opinion?
qh: 1903 और 1905 के बीच नरमपंथी नेतृत्व द्वारा शुरू किए गए शुरुआती विभाजन-विरोधी आंदोलन ने जनमत तैयार करने के लिए मुख्य रूप से किस संचार साधन पर भरोसा किया?
o: Propaganda through newspapers such as Hitabadi, Sanjibani, and Bengalee
Organizing secret underground revolutionary parameter tracking societies
The total structural boycott of all provincial legislative councils instantly
Launching an armed paramilitary movement armed with traditional clubs
e: Detailed Explanation: The Moderate methodology was focused on creating educated public opinion in India and England. For this propaganda, they continuously utilized influential newspapers like Hitabadi, Sanjibani, and Bengalee.

qe: In which month and year did the colonial government officially ignore public opposition and formally announce the implementation of the partition of Bengal, triggering immediate local protest pledges?
qh: किस महीने और वर्ष में औपनिवेशिक सरकार ने आधिकारिक तौर पर जनविरोध की अनदेखी की और औपचारिक रूप से बंगाल के विभाजन के कार्यान्वयन की घोषणा की, जिससे तत्काल स्थानीय विरोध प्रदर्शन शुरू हो गए?
o: July 1905
December 1903
August 1905
October 1905
e: Detailed Explanation: Despite extensive petitions, the government formally announced the partition plan in July 1905. This sparked immediate widespread outrage, and localized protest meetings in small towns across Bengal first took the pledge to boycott foreign goods.

qe: The formal proclamation of the historic Swadeshi Movement was made on August 7, 1905, following the passage of the Boycott Resolution at which landmark meeting?
qh: बायकाट प्रस्ताव (Boycott Resolution) पारित होने के बाद 7 अगस्त, 1905 को किस ऐतिहासिक बैठक में ऐतिहासिक स्वदेशी आंदोलन की औपचारिक घोषणा की गई थी?
o: A massive meeting held in the Calcutta Townhall
The annual national session convened at Gokuldas Tejpal Sanskrit College
A regional protest assembly organized at the public Chawdar tank
An open-air volunteer convention hosted inside Fergusson College, Pune
e: Detailed Explanation: On August 7, 1905, a massive public meeting was held at the Calcutta Townhall. The historic Boycott Resolution was passed here, marking the formal proclamation and launch of the Swadeshi Movement.

qe: Following the townhall proclamation of the Swadeshi Movement, nationalist leaders quickly dispersed across the province to propagate the message of boycotting which specific British import goods?
qh: स्वदेशी आंदोलन की टाउनहॉल घोषणा के बाद, राष्ट्रवादी नेता किस विशिष्ट ब्रिटिश आयातित वस्तुओं के बहिष्कार के संदेश को प्रसारित करने के लिए पूरे प्रांत में तेजी से फैल गए?
o: Manchester cloth and Liverpool salt
Foreign non-ionic liquid detergents and dyes
Superconducting machinery tools and steel tracks
Opium shipments and sugarcane agricultural inputs
e: Detailed Explanation: The core economic tactic of the early Swadeshi movement was hitting British commercial interests directly. Leaders traveled to different districts to preach the total boycott of Manchester-manufactured cloth and Liverpool-produced salt.

qe: On October 16, 1905, the partition of Bengal formally came into force. How was this specific landmark day observed by the public across Bengal to register their resistance?
qh: 16 अक्टूबर, 1905 को बंगाल का विभाजन औपचारिक रूप से लागू हुआ। जनता ने अपना विरोध दर्ज कराने के लिए बंगाल भर में इस विशिष्ट ऐतिहासिक दिन को किस रूप में मनाया?
o: As a day of mourning where people fasted, bathed in the Ganga, and walked barefoot in processions
By launching an immediate armed parameters conflict against the local police
Through the complete permanent migration of the working class toward Bihar plains
By convening an extra-ordinary secret session of the Federal judicial court
e: Detailed Explanation: October 16, 1905, was observed as a collective day of mourning. The public fasted, wore black bands, bathed in the Ganga, and marched barefoot in massive silent processions as a symbol of grief and resistance.

qe: Which celebrated patriotic song, composed by Rabindranath Tagore during the anti-partition processions, later became the national anthem of present-day Bangladesh?
qh: विभाजन-विरोधी जुलूसों के दौरान रवींद्रनाथ टैगोर द्वारा रचित कौन सा प्रसिद्ध देशभक्ति गीत बाद में वर्तमान बांग्लादेश का राष्ट्रीय गान बना?
o: Amar Sonar Bangla
Bande Mataram
Jana Gana Mana
Sare Jahan Se Achha
e: Detailed Explanation: Rabindranath Tagore composed 'Amar Sonar Bangla' during the height of the anti-partition movement. It was sung by marching crowds in the streets of Calcutta and was later adopted as the national anthem of Bangladesh.

qe: What unique fraternal ritual did the people of Bengal perform on October 16, 1905, to symbolize the underlying, unbreakable unity of the two partitioned halves of the province?
qh: बंगाल के लोगों ने 16 अक्टूबर, 1905 को प्रांत के दोनों विभाजित हिस्सों की अंतर्निहित, अटूट एकता का प्रतीक बनाने के लिए कौन सा अनूठा भाईचारे का अनुष्ठान किया था?
o: They tied rakhis on each other's hands
They mixed soil solutions from eastern and western districts into a single vase
They completely burned copies of the newly amended Registration Act publicly
They distributed non-caloric artificial sweeteners inside local temples
e: Detailed Explanation: At the suggestion of Rabindranath Tagore, the day of partition was celebrated as Rakhi Bandhan day. People tied rakhis on each other's wrists as a symbolic declaration that the artificial administrative borders drawn by the British could not splinter the emotional unity of Bengalis.

qe: Later in the day on October 16, 1905, Surendranath Banerjea and Ananda Mohan Bose addressed a massive nationalist gathering. How much capital was spontaneously raised for the movement within a few hours of this meeting?
qh: 16 अक्टूबर, 1905 को बाद में सुरेन्द्रनाथ बनर्जी और आनंद मोहन बोस ने एक विशाल राष्ट्रवादी सभा को संबोधित किया। इस बैठक के कुछ ही घंटों के भीतर आंदोलन के लिए स्वतः ही कितनी पूंजी जुटाई गई थी?
e: Detailed Explanation: The public meeting addressed by Banerjea and Bose on the afternoon of October 16 drew immense crowds. Reflecting the intense public support, a sum of Rs 50,000 was spontaneously collected within a few hours to fund the Swadeshi struggle.

qe: The Swadeshi Movement quickly expanded beyond the borders of Bengal. Which nationalist leaders successfully spearheaded the movement in Poona and Bombay?
qh: स्वदेशी आंदोलन तेजी से बंगाल की सीमाओं से बाहर फैल गया। किन राष्ट्रवादी नेताओं ने पूना और बॉम्बे में इस आंदोलन का सफलतापूर्वक नेतृत्व किया था?
o: Bal Gangadhar Tilak
Lala Lajpat Rai and Ajit Singh
Syed Haider Raza
Chidambaram Pillai
e: Detailed Explanation: Lokmanya Bal Gangadhar Tilak recognized the national potential of the anti-partition cause and successfully introduced and led the Swadeshi and boycott campaign across Poona and the Bombay Presidency.

qe: The message of Swadeshi and boycott of foreign goods was actively carried to the North-Western regions of India. Who organized the movement in Punjab?
qh: स्वदेशी और विदेशी वस्तुओं के बहिष्कार का संदेश सक्रिय रूप से भारत के उत्तर-पश्चिमी क्षेत्रों में ले जाया गया था। पंजाब में इस आंदोलन का आयोजन किसने किया था?
o: Lala Lajpat Rai and Ajit Singh
Syed Haider Raza
Chidambaram Pillai
Gopal Krishna Gokhale
e: Detailed Explanation: In Punjab, the anti-partition and Swadeshi message was powerfully propagated through public mobilization led by Lala Lajpat Rai and Sardar Ajit Singh (the uncle of Bhagat Singh).

qe: Which distinct nationalist leader was responsible for organizing the administrative core of the Swadeshi Movement within Delhi?
qh: दिल्ली के भीतर स्वदेशी आंदोलन के प्रशासनिक कोर को संगठित करने के लिए कौन सा विशिष्ट राष्ट्रवादी नेता जिम्मेदार था?
o: Syed Haider Raza
Chidambaram Pillai
Ananda Mohan Bose
K.K. Mitra
e: Detailed Explanation: The Swadeshi movement expanded into a pan-Indian phenomenon. In Delhi, the public agitations and boycott campaigns were led and structured by Syed Haider Raza.

qe: The Southern maritime regions of India also witnessed powerful Swadeshi agitations. Who spearheaded the movement within the Madras Presidency?
qh: भारत के दक्षिणी समुद्री क्षेत्रों में भी शक्तिशाली स्वदेशी आंदोलन देखे गए। मद्रास प्रेसीडेंसी के भीतर इस आंदोलन का नेतृत्व किसने किया था?
o: Chidambaram Pillai
Gopal Krishna Gokhale
Surendranath Banerjea
Aurobindo Ghosh
e: Detailed Explanation: In the Madras Presidency, the Swadeshi campaign and nationalist public speeches were powerfully organized under the leadership of Chidambaram Pillai (who famously launched the Swadeshi Steam Navigation Company).

qe: The Indian National Congress met in 1905 under the presidentship of Gopal Krishna Gokhale. What specific formal resolutions were passed during this annual session?
qh: भारतीय राष्ट्रीय कांग्रेस की बैठक 1905 में गोपाल कृष्ण गोखले की अध्यक्षता में हुई थी। इस वार्षिक सत्र के दौरान कौन से विशिष्ट औपचारिक प्रस्ताव पारित किए गए थे?
o: To condemn the partition of Bengal and the reactionary policies of Curzon, and to support the Swadeshi Movement of Bengal
To declare absolute immediate independence and initiate armed guerrilla conflicts across provinces
To completely merge the Congress infrastructure with the orthodox Dharma Sabha coalition
To mandate the exclusive use of English language instead of vernaculars inside all district boards
e: Detailed Explanation: The 1905 Banaras session of the Congress, presided over by the Moderate leader G.K. Gokhale, formally resolved to condemn Curzon's reactionary administration and the partition of Bengal, while extending official support to the ongoing Swadeshi movement within Bengal.

qe: During the 1905 Congress session, a tactical divide emerged regarding the scope of the movement. What expansion did militant nationalists like Tilak, Lajpat Rai, and Bipin Chandra Pal advocate?
qh: 1905 के कांग्रेस सत्र के दौरान, आंदोलन के दायरे को लेकर एक रणनीतिक विभाजन सामने आया। तिलक, लाजपत राय और विपिन चंद्र पाल जैसे उग्रवादी राष्ट्रवादियों ने किस विस्तार की वकालत की थी?
o: To take the movement outside Bengal to other parts of the country and transform it into a full-fledged political mass struggle for Swaraj
To restrict all active boycott agitations strictly to the municipal limits of Calcutta townhall
To request the British Crown to completely dissolve the provincial legislative councils permanently
To completely halt any ongoing vernacular publication propaganda channels
e: Detailed Explanation: The Extremists (militant nationalists) wanted to expand the movement beyond Bengal to make it a truly pan-Indian mass struggle. They advocated moving past a simple economic boycott of goods to launch a full-fledged political mass resistance with the ultimate goal of attaining Swaraj.

qe: A historic constitutional declaration was made at the Calcutta Congress session of 1906 under the presidentship of Dadabhai Naoroji. What was officially declared as the central goal of the Indian National Congress?
qh: दादाभाई नौरोजी की अध्यक्षता में 1906 के कलकत्ता कांग्रेस सत्र में एक ऐतिहासिक संवैधानिक घोषणा की गई थी। भारतीय राष्ट्रीय कांग्रेस के मुख्य लक्ष्य के रूप में आधिकारिक तौर पर क्या घोषित किया गया था?
o: Self-government or Swaraj like the United Kingdom or its colonies of Australia and Canada
The direct administrative replacement of the Viceroy by a British Cabinet Secretary of State exclusively
A complete integration of local agrarian fields with international financial market prices
The mandatory implementation of non-competitive allosteric inhibitors inside all local schools
e: Detailed Explanation: At the Calcutta session of 1906, Dadabhai Naoroji used his presidential platform to declare that the ultimate goal of the Congress was 'self-government or Swaraj', explicitly modeled on the autonomous status enjoyed by self-governing British colonies like Canada and Australia.

qe: The ideological deadlock between the Moderates and Extremists regarding the pace and techniques of struggle culminated in a historic party split. At which session did this split occur?
qh: संघर्ष की गति और तकनीकों के संबंध में नरमपंथियों और गरमपंथियों के बीच वैचारिक गतिरोध के परिणामस्वरूप एक ऐतिहासिक पार्टी विभाजन हुआ। यह विभाजन किस सत्र में हुआ था?
o: The Surat session of 1907
The Calcutta session of 1906
The Banaras session of 1905
The Lucknow session of 1916
e: Detailed Explanation: The growing rift over leadership and methodologies reached an absolute deadlock at the Surat session of 1907. The resulting 'Surat Split' severely weakened the organizational unity of the national movement and had serious negative consequences for the Swadeshi Movement.

qe: After 1905, why did the Extremist leadership acquire a dominant influence over the Swadeshi Movement within Bengal, shifting it away from the Moderate path?
qh: 1905 के बाद, बंगाल के भीतर स्वदेशी आंदोलन पर गरमदलीय (Extremist) नेतृत्व ने एक प्रमुख प्रभाव क्यों प्राप्त किया, जिससे यह नरमपंथी मार्ग से दूर हो गया?
o: The Moderate-led petitions failed to yield concrete results, and the government resorted to severe suppressive measures
The Moderates voluntarily resigned from their positions to join the orthodox Dharma Sabha
The British administration provided massive financial subsidies exclusively to Extremist journals
The local village moneylenders completely liquidated all peasant debts inside the western half
e: Detailed Explanation: The Extremists gained dominance because the traditional Moderate methods of petitions and memoranda failed to stop the implementation of the partition. Furthermore, the divisive tactics of the state and its brutal suppression of student protestors embittered the public, turning them toward radical options.

qe: To crush the Swadeshi Movement, the colonial government deployed highly suppressive measures against the student population. Which of the following highlights a measure they used?
qh: स्वदेशी आंदोलन को कुचलने के लिए औपनिवेशिक सरकार ने छात्र आबादी के खिलाफ अत्यधिक दमनकारी उपाय अपनाए। निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा उनके द्वारा उपयोग किए जाने वाले उपाय को रेखांकित करता है?
o: Inflicting corporal punishment on students and restricting their enrollment privileges
Providing free advanced technical education grants exclusively to non-official Indian student groups
Forcing all student volunteers to compile bilingual dictionaries in classical Sanskrit loops
Mandating that every student must ingest non-caloric artificial sweetening agents daily
e: Detailed Explanation: The state targeted students because they were the backbone of picket lines and processions. Suppressive measures included inflicting brutal corporal punishment on young students, rusticating them from schools, and threatening institutions with the withdrawal of grants.

qe: As part of its suppressive campaign against nationalist expressions, what cultural restriction did the colonial government legally enforce in public spaces?
qh: राष्ट्रवादी अभिव्यक्तियों के खिलाफ अपने दमनकारी अभियान के हिस्से के रूप में, औपनिवेशिक सरकार ने सार्वजनिक स्थानों पर कौन सा सांस्कृतिक प्रतिबंध कानूनी रूप से लागू किया था?
o: A total ban on the public singing of Vande Mataram
The absolute prohibition of using local vernacular languages in commerce trade
A mandatory registration rule forcing people to carry standard red books everywhere
A ban on the manufacturing of traditional soft potassium cosmetic soaps
e: Detailed Explanation: To suppress the emotional tide of the movement, the government passed circulars that placed a complete ban on the public singing of the patriotic song 'Vande Mataram', treating it as an act of sedition.

qe: The comprehensive 'Passive Resistance' program outlined by the Extremist leadership went far beyond a simple boycott of British cloth. What did this expanded strategy explicitly include?
qh: गरमदलीय नेतृत्व द्वारा रेखांकित व्यापक 'निष्क्रिय प्रतिरोध' (Passive Resistance) कार्यक्रम ब्रिटिश कपड़ों के एक साधारण बहिष्कार से बहुत आगे निकल गया। इस विस्तारित रणनीति में स्पष्ट रूप से क्या शामिल था?
o: A boycott of government schools, colleges, government service, courts, legislative councils, and titles
The systematic destruction of all primary agricultural fields across the eastern half
Filing joint civil lawsuits inside the Federal Court benches against the Secretary of State
An absolute requirement to replace all local municipal boards with secret religious sabhas
e: Detailed Explanation: The Extremist program focused on non-cooperation and passive resistance. They called upon citizens to boycott government-run educational institutions, colonial administrative services, British law courts, legislative councils, municipalities, and government-awarded titles.

qe: Who among the Extremist ideologues brilliantly defined the purpose of passive resistance as an organized refusal to help British officialdom, stating that 'Political freedom is the lifebreath of a nation'?
qh: गरमदलीय विचारकों में से किसने निष्क्रिय प्रतिरोध के उद्देश्य को ब्रिटिश अधिकारियों की मदद करने से एक संगठित इनकार के रूप में परिभाषित किया था, और कहा था कि 'राजनीतिक स्वतंत्रता एक राष्ट्र की जीवन सांस है'?
o: Aurobindo Ghosh
Bal Gangadhar Tilak
Surendranath Banerjea
Dadabhai Naoroji
e: Detailed Explanation: Aurobindo Ghosh was the key philosophical architect of the passive resistance program. He wrote extensively that the goal was to make British administration impossible through an organized refusal to cooperate, famously declaring that political freedom is essential to a nation's life.

qe: A logistics routing path loops through a right-angled triangle mapping. A transport car travels 60 km North from junction O, and then drives 11 km East to reach storage point S. Find the straight-line distance from O to S.
qh: एक परिवहन कार जंक्शन O से 60 किमी उत्तर की ओर चलती है, और फिर पूर्व की ओर 11 किमी जाकर भंडारण बिंदु S पर पहुँचती है। O से S की सीधी रेखा की दूरी ज्ञात कीजिए।
o: 61 km
71 km
65 km
63 km
e:
Detailed Explanation: This spatial path sets up a classic right-angled triangle configuration with legs measuring 60 km and 11 km. The straight-line distance is the hypotenuse.
Applying the Pythagoras theorem: $\text{Distance} = \sqrt{60^2 + 11^2} = \sqrt{3600 + 121} = \sqrt{3721} = \mathbf{61\text{ km}}$.

qe: In a biological ecosystem study tracking energy metrics, if the Net Primary Productivity (NPP) of a forest tract is measured at 24,000 units and the energy lost during plant respiration (R) is 16,000 units, calculate the Gross Primary Productivity (GPP).
qh: ऊर्जा मानकों पर नज़र रखने वाले एक जैविक पारितंत्र अध्ययन में, यदि एक वन क्षेत्र की शुद्ध प्राथमिक उत्पादकता (NPP) 24,000 इकाइयाँ मापी जाती है और पौधों के श्वसन (R) के दौरान खर्च की गई ऊर्जा 16,000 इकाइयाँ है, तो सकल प्राथमिक उत्पादकता (GPP) की गणना करें।
o: 40,000 units
8,000 units
32,000 units
48,000 units
e:
Detailed Explanation: Utilizing the baseline ecological energy flow equation: $NPP = GPP - R$, we rewrite it to isolate Gross Primary Productivity: $GPP = NPP + R$.
Substituting the values: $GPP = 24,000 + 16,000 = \mathbf{40,000\text{ units}}$.

qe: The viceroy who masterminded the partition of Bengal attempted to win over Muslim communalists by offering a specific political vision for Dacca. Who was this viceroy?
qh: बंगाल के विभाजन की योजना बनाने वाले वायसराय ने ढाका के लिए एक विशिष्ट राजनीतिक दृष्टिकोण की पेशकश करके मुस्लिम सांप्रदायिकों को अपने पक्ष में करने का प्रयास किया था। यह वायसराय कौन था?
o: Lord Curzon
Lord Wellesley
Lord William Bentinck
Lord Ripon
e: Detailed Explanation: Lord Curzon was the Viceroy of India who engineered the partition plan. He toured eastern Bengal and explicitly gave speeches to woo Muslims, arguing that making Dacca the capital of a new Muslim-majority province would restore a sense of unity they had not experienced since the days of old Muslim kings.

qe: The theme song that almost spontaneously became the standard anthem of the entire anti-partition and Swadeshi Movement, sung by crowds during barefoot processions, was:
qh: वह विषय गीत जो लगभग स्वतः ही पूरे विभाजन-विरोधी और स्वदेशी आंदोलन का मानक गान बन गया, और जिसे नंगे पैर जुलूसों के दौरान भीड़ द्वारा गाया जाता था, वह था:
o: Bande Mataram
Amar Sonar Bangla
Jana Gana Mana
Sare Jahan Se Achha
e: Detailed Explanation: Bankim Chandra Chatterjee's 'Bande Mataram' became the definitive theme song of the Swadeshi Movement. It was sung by thousands of people as they marched through the streets in barefoot protest processions across Bengal.

qe: The Indian National Congress session hosted at Calcutta in 1906 is highly significant because its declaration directly influenced the Extremist program. Who presided over this historic session?
qh: 1906 में कलकत्ता में आयोजित भारतीय राष्ट्रीय कांग्रेस का सत्र अत्यधिक महत्वपूर्ण है क्योंकि इसकी घोषणा ने सीधे गरमदलीय कार्यक्रम को प्रभावित किया था। इस ऐतिहासिक सत्र की अध्यक्षता किसने की थी?
o: Dadabhai Naoroji
Gopal Krishna Gokhale
Bal Gangadhar Tilak
Surendranath Banerjea
e: Detailed Explanation: The 1906 Calcutta session of the Congress was presided over by the venerable leader Dadabhai Naoroji. His presidential declaration designating self-government or Swaraj as the ultimate goal of the Congress gave structural validation to the radical programs of the Extremists.

qe: What was the primary long-term strategic objective shared by both the Moderate and Extremist factions within the Swadeshi Movement, despite their deep disputes over pace and techniques?
qh: गति और तकनीकों पर उनके गहरे विवादों के बावजूद, स्वदेशी आंदोलन के भीतर नरमपंथी और गरमपंथी दोनों गुटों द्वारा साझा किया गया प्राथमिक दीर्घकालिक रणनीतिक उद्देश्य क्या था?
o: The ultimate reversal of the partition of Bengal and the structural advancement of the nation
The complete conversion of all local schools into English-only military academies
Forcing the central government to permanently freeze the functions of the Supreme Court
The systematic preservation of the socio-economic inequalities managed by local zamindars
e: Detailed Explanation: Despite their programmatic deadlock at Surat over the pace of the agitation, both the Moderates and Extremists shared the core goals of reversing the partition of Bengal and achieving self-governing advancement for the country.

qe: Under the passive resistance strategy, the slogan of absolute independence from foreign rule was given a central place in national politics. According to the Extremist ideology, this goal was to be achieved through:
qh: निष्क्रिय प्रतिरोध रणनीति के तहत, विदेशी शासन से पूर्ण स्वतंत्रता के नारे को राष्ट्रीय राजनीति में एक केंद्रीय स्थान दिया गया था। गरमदलीय विचारधारा के अनुसार, इस लक्ष्य को किसके माध्यम से प्राप्त किया जाना था?
o: Self-sacrifice and organized mass non-cooperation
Filing formal legal petitions regularly before the British Parliament
Securing administrative concession titles from the Viceroy's executive council
The physical structural relocation of all national headquarters to London directly
e: Detailed Explanation: The militant nationalists (Extremists) believed that political freedom could not be achieved through minor administrative concessions or prayers. They introduced the concept of mass non-cooperation and emphasized that the ultimate goal of absolute independence must be won through mass self-sacrifice and relentless passive resistance.
